title: Parking lot allocation
instructions:
Implement a deterministic parking lot allocator in `parking.py`.

A spot has one of the kinds `"compact"`, `"standard"`, `"large"`, ranked in that order. A vehicle of a given kind fits in spots of that kind or larger. When parking, choose the smallest compatible free kind, then the lexicographically smallest spot ID within that kind.

Public API:
- `ParkingLot(spots: dict[str, str])`: map nonempty string spot IDs to kinds. Empty lots are allowed. Unknown kinds or empty IDs raise `ValueError`. Copy the mapping so later caller mutations have no effect.
- `park(plate: str, kind: str) -> str | None`: return the allocated spot ID, or None if none fits. Empty plates, unknown kinds, or an already parked plate raise `ValueError` without changing the lot, even if full. A failed allocation does not register the plate. Plates are case sensitive.
- `leave(plate: str) -> str`: free that vehicle's spot and return its ID. An absent plate raises `KeyError`.
- `locate(plate: str) -> str | None`: return the plate's spot, or None if absent.
- `snapshot() -> list[tuple[str, str, str | None]]`: list every spot as `(spot_id, kind, plate_or_none)`, sorted lexicographically by spot ID. The returned list is independent of future lot changes.

All IDs, plates, and kinds supplied are strings. A nonempty string containing spaces is valid; do not strip strings. Do not change existing assignments when another vehicle arrives or leaves. Helper functions may be private and are not tested directly.

### Files
- `parking.py`: implement `ParkingLot` and any allocation/validation helpers.
